title: Tropisms & photoperiodism
group: BIO-EVOL / BIO-ECOL / BIO-PLANT — Evolution, Ecology & Plants
examples: What is the difference between phototropism and gravitropism?
How does the length of day affect flowering in plants?
Where in the plant does the auxin hormone work?

explain.say: Today we will learn about how plants react to light.
Phototropism is the bending of a plant towards a light source.

items: Stem grows faster on shaded side

explain.say: Auxin is a plant hormone that controls cell elongation.
When auxin moves to the shaded side, it promotes faster growth there.
Some plants flower best when days are short, called short-day plants.
Other plants need long days to produce flowers, long-day plants.

faq.q: What is the main difference between phototropism and gravitropism?
faq.a: Phototropism is growth in response to light, while gravitropism is growth in response to gravity. You might also ask about light bending or gravity bending.
asks: How does light affect roots versus shoots?
What causes plants to bend downwards?
Is phototropism the same as tropism?

faq.q: If I grow a plant in complete darkness, what will happen to it?
faq.a: The plant will not exhibit phototropism because there is no light gradient to follow. It will still grow, but it will be etiolated.
asks: Does light cause plants to bend?
What happens to plants without sun?

faq.q: What is the role of auxin in plant development?
faq.a: Auxin is a key plant hormone that controls cell elongation by promoting cell wall loosening. It is responsible for many directional growths.
asks: What does auxin do inside a plant cell?

faq.q: Why do some plants only flower in the fall?
faq.a: This is because they are short-day plants, meaning they need a period of darkness longer than a critical length to trigger flowering. They are sensitive to night length.
asks: What determines when a plant flowers?
Do all plants flower at the same time?
What is the role of day length?

faq.q: What does 'photoperiodism' mean in simple terms?
faq.a: It means that a plant's life cycle, like flowering, is controlled by the length of the day or night. The plant measures the duration of darkness.
asks: What is the relationship between light and bloom?
Does time of day affect plant life?

facts: Phototropism is the directional growth of a plant in response to light.
Auxin is a plant hormone that promotes cell elongation.
Short-day plants flower when the night period is longer than a certain length.
Long-day plants require a night period shorter than a certain length to flower.

quiz.say: A plant stem bends towards a bright window. This bending is an example of:
quiz.why: Phototropism is the specific growth response of a plant towards a light source.

wrong.0: Gravitropism relates to gravity, not light direction.
wrong.1: Auxin is the chemical that causes the bending, but phototropism is the name for the process.
wrong.2: Photoperiodism relates to day length, not light direction.

quiz.say: A plant needs a long period of darkness to flower. This plant is classified as:
quiz.why: Short-day plants are defined by their need for a long night period to initiate flowering.

wrong.0: This describes a hormone requirement, not the day length requirement.
wrong.2: Long-day plants need a shorter night period to flower.
wrong.3: This term describes light bending, not flowering time.

quiz.say: If a plant's flowering is controlled by the length of the night, what process is being demonstrated?
quiz.why: Photoperiodism is the term for flowering being regulated by the relative length of day and night.

wrong.0: Phototropism describes bending towards light, not flowering time.
wrong.1: This describes the uneven distribution of the hormone auxin.
wrong.2: Etiolation is the process of growing in the dark, which is a result, not the control mechanism.
